name: Pregabalin

lead: Pregabalin (Lyrica) is a prescription gabapentinoid approved for neuropathic pain, fibromyalgia and add-on seizure treatment, and licensed for generalized anxiety disorder in some regions. On looksmax.org, users describe taking it to feel less inhibited and appear more relaxed and confident socially.

It binds the alpha-2-delta subunit of voltage-gated calcium channels, reducing release of excitatory neurotransmitters such as glutamate. User accounts are anecdotal; no trial has tested it for social presence in people without a diagnosed condition.

paras: Forum users describe taking it before social situations to ease inhibition, and some swap questions about obtaining it and about withdrawal. Medically it is taken on a prescribed schedule for its approved conditions.

The label warns of respiratory depression with other CNS depressants, suicidal thoughts, angioedema, dizziness, somnolence, peripheral edema, weight gain and withdrawal reactions after abrupt stopping. It is Schedule V in the US, and reference sources note misuse potential.

angle.text: Forum posters take pregabalin to lower social anxiety and inhibition, aiming to come across as more relaxed, outgoing and confident. It is approved for nerve pain, fibromyalgia and seizures.

lead: Pregabalin is a prescription gabapentinoid, structurally related to GABA, sold by Pfizer as Lyrica. The US label lists diabetic peripheral neuropathic pain, postherpetic neuralgia, fibromyalgia, spinal-cord-injury neuropathic pain and adjunctive treatment of partial-onset seizures [1][2].

In looksmaxxing forums it is discussed mainly as a social-disinhibition or anxiety-relief drug; users on looksmax.org have described taking it before social situations and have exchanged questions about obtaining it and about withdrawal [3][4]. These accounts are anecdotal, and no published trial has tested pregabalin for this purpose in people without a diagnosed condition.

Grokipedia reports that pregabalin is a Schedule V controlled substance in the US and that its euphoric and sedative effects at high amounts have led to concerns about misuse [1]. The label warns of respiratory depression with other CNS depressants, suicidal ideation, angioedema and withdrawal effects after abrupt discontinuation [2].

paras: Grokipedia reports the FDA first approved pregabalin on 30 December 2004 for adjunctive therapy in partial-onset seizures and postherpetic neuralgia, followed by diabetic neuropathic pain in 2005 and fibromyalgia in 2007 [1]. The current US label also lists neuropathic pain associated with spinal cord injury and adjunctive seizure therapy from one month of age [2]. In some regions it is also licensed for generalized anxiety disorder [1].

Neuropathic pain guidelines from international and European groups place pregabalin among first-line options [5][6][7]. Systematic reviews of neuropathic pain drugs include pregabalin in their rankings [5]. A guideline on chronic cough has also considered gabapentinoids [8].

Pregabalin binds with high affinity to the alpha-2-delta subunit of voltage-gated calcium channels, which is thought to reduce release of excitatory neurotransmitters; the mechanism is not fully established [1]. Grokipedia contrasts it with gabapentin, noting higher and more predictable oral bioavailability [1].

The label lists angioedema, hypersensitivity, suicidal behavior and ideation, respiratory depression with concomitant CNS depressants, dizziness and somnolence, withdrawal effects after abrupt or rapid discontinuation, peripheral edema and weight gain [2]. Grokipedia additionally reports sexual dysfunction (decreased libido, erectile dysfunction, abnormal orgasm) among reported adverse effects [1].
Grokipedia reports that pregabalin is classified as Schedule V in the US [1].

On looksmax.org, threads describe pregabalin as a drug for lowering inhibition in people with social anxiety; one user reported obtaining it through a clinic visit and described feeling relaxed and talkative afterwards [3]. Other threads ask about withdrawal symptoms [4]. Forum participants also discuss acquiring it from outside prescription channels; the wiki does not document sourcing. Clinicians and regulators describe these as off-label or non-medical uses with misuse and withdrawal risks [1][2].

A 2003 randomized placebo-controlled trial examined pregabalin for postherpetic neuralgia [9]. Meta-analyses and guidelines on neuropathic pain assess pregabalin among first-line drugs [5][6][7]. Registered trials include dose-response work in restless legs syndrome, once-daily formulations for partial seizures, post-mastectomy pain studies and a large Korean post-marketing surveillance study [10][11][12][13]. No studies were found testing pregabalin for social disinhibition or appearance outcomes in people without a diagnosed condition.
